title: The budget review
scenario: Your team runs two AI features: a live support chat and a nightly job that summarises the day's tickets for managers. Finance wants a monthly estimate for the chat and a plan to cut cost. Use the example prices and traffic in the exhibit (the prices are made up for this case, not a real price list).
exhibit:
EXAMPLE PRICES (made up for this case)
  input   $3.00 per 1M tokens
  output  $15.00 per 1M tokens

LIVE CHAT (per day)
  conversations                      2,000
  avg input tokens / conversation    5,000
  avg output tokens / conversation     500
  every request starts with the same 3,000-token policy doc,
  but the template puts the user's question BEFORE the doc

NIGHTLY SUMMARY JOB
  starts at 18:00; managers read it at 09:00 the day after next (39 hours later)
  currently: one live API call per ticket

SWITCH TEST
  reasoning model: usage shows 4,000 output tokens
  for replies of about 150 visible words

questions.prompt: What is the chat's estimated cost for a 30-day month at the example prices?

options.explanation: That is one day. The question asks for a 30-day month.
That prices output at the input rate (11 MTok × $3 a day). Output has its own, higher price.
That is ten times too high. Check the conversion: 10,000,000 tokens is 10 MTok, not 100.

questions.prompt: Every chat request repeats the same 3,000-token policy doc. What is the best change?

options.text: Put the static policy doc first and the question last, so prompt caching can reuse the prefix.
options.explanation: Right. Caching needs the prefix to match. OpenAI caches automatically on supported models; Anthropic cache reads cost a fraction of base input. Either way, static content must come first.

options.text: Keep the question first; caching matches any part of the prompt, wherever the change sits.
options.explanation: Caching works on the prefix. The OpenAI docs say the entire rendered prefix must match, so a changing question at the start breaks reuse.

options.text: Remove the policy doc and trust the model's general knowledge to answer the policy questions.
options.explanation: That saves tokens but loses the grounding the answers need. Caching cuts the cost and keeps the doc.

options.text: Send the policy doc only on the first turn of each conversation, then drop it from later turns.
options.explanation: The APIs are stateless. A doc missing from a request is not available to the model for that request.

questions.prompt: The nightly summary job starts at 18:00 and is read 39 hours later. How should it run?

options.text: As a batch job, for about 50% off on both vendors.
options.explanation: Right. Both vendors document a 50% Batch API discount. The OpenAI docs say each batch finishes inside 24 hours, so the job fits as long as the deadline is more than 24 hours after the start.

options.text: As live calls with streaming, so it finishes faster.
options.explanation: Nobody is watching the job run. Streaming helps users see text early; it does not reduce cost.

options.text: As live calls on the largest model, for best quality.
options.explanation: That is the most expensive choice for work that can wait. Batch first, then pick the cheapest model that still passes.

options.text: Split it into many parallel live calls to finish within minutes.
options.explanation: Parallel live calls pay full price and use your live rate limits. Batch is cheaper and has its own limit pool on OpenAI.

questions.prompt: In the switch test, a reasoning model reports 4,000 output tokens for about 150 visible words. Why?

options.text: Reasoning tokens are not shown in the reply but are billed as output tokens.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say reasoning tokens are not visible but are billed as output; Claude thinking tokens are billed as output too. Estimate with usage, not visible text.

options.text: The usage block is wrong; bill by visible words.
options.explanation: usage is the real count. Hidden reasoning is part of the output you pay for.

options.text: Output tokens include the input prompt.
options.explanation: Input and output are counted separately. The extra output is reasoning.

options.text: The 150 words are billed twice: once as output and once as context for the next turn.
options.explanation: This is the usage of one reply, and output is billed once, when it is generated. The extra tokens are hidden reasoning.
